regions.name: Nord-Est
regions.title: Nord-Est (department)
text: Nord-Est (French, pronounced [nɔʁɛst] ) or Nodès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "North East") is one of the ten departments of Haiti, located in northern Haiti. It has an area of 1,623 km2 (627 sq mi), making it the smallest of all the departments. It had an estimated population of 393,967 as of 2015. Its capital is Fort-Liberté. It was a part of the Nord department.

regions.name: Centre
regions.title: Centre (department)
text: Centre (French, pronounced [sɑ̃tʁ] ) or Sant (Haitian Creole; both meaning "Center") is the only landlocked department (French: départements; Haitian Creole: depatman) of Haiti, located in the center of the country along the border with the Dominican Republic. As of 2015, its estimated population was 746,236. Its capital is Hinche.

Centre was established in 1962 during François Duvalier's territorial reorganization. It is the third-largest department of Haiti, and is divided into four arrondissements and 12 communes. The Peligre Dam, the largest hydroelectric dam on Hispaniola, is located in the department and provides water to Artibonite.

regions.name: Ouest
regions.title: Ouest (department)
text: Ouest (French, pronounced [wɛst] ) or Lwès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "West") is one of the ten departments of Haiti. It is located in south-central Haiti, linking the Great-North and the Tiburon Peninsula.
It is the jurisdictional seat of the national capital, the city of Port-au-Prince.

regions.name: Sud-Est
regions.title: Sud-Est (department)
text: Sud-Est (French, pronounced [sydɛst] ) or Sidès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "South East") is one of the ten departments of Haiti located in southern Haiti. It has an area of 2,034.10 km2 and a population of 632,601 (2015). Its capital is Jacmel.

regions.name: Sud
regions.title: Sud (department)
text: Sud (French, pronounced [syd] ) or Sid (Haitian Creole; both meaning "South") is one of the ten departments of Haiti and located in southern Haiti. It has an area of 2,653.60 square kilometres (1,024.56 sq mi) and a population of 774,976. Its capital is Les Cayes.

regions.name: Grand'Anse
regions.title: Grand'Anse (department)
text: Grand'Anse (, French: [ɡʁɑ̃tɑ̃s]), Grandans or Grantans (Haitian Creole: [ɡɣãtãs]; both meaning "Big Cove") is one of the ten departments of Haiti. Its capital is Jérémie.

regions.name: Nord-Ouest
regions.title: Nord-Ouest (department)
text: Nord-Ouest (French, pronounced [nɔʁwɛst] ) or Nòdwès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "North West") is one of the ten departments of Haiti as well as the northernmost one. It has an area of 2,102.88 km2 (811.93 sq mi) and a population of 728,807 (2015 Census). Its capital is Port-de-Paix.

regions.name: Nord
regions.title: Nord (Haitian department)
text: Nord (French, pronounced [nɔʁ] ) or Nò (Haitian Creole, pronounced [nɔ]; both meaning "North") is one of the ten departments of Haiti and located in northern Haiti. It has an area of 2,114.91 km2 (816.57 sq mi) and a population of 1,067,177 (2015). Its capital is Cap-Haïtien.

regions.name: Artibonite
regions.title: Artibonite (department)
text: Artibonite (French pronunciation: [aʁtibɔnit]; Haitian Creole: Latibonit) is one of the ten departments of Haiti located in central Haiti. With an area of 4,887 km2 it is Haiti's largest department. As of 2015, its estimated population was 1,727,524. The region is the country's main rice-growing area. The main cities are Gonaïves (the capital) and Saint-Marc. In February 2004 an insurgency tried unsuccessfully to declare Artibonite's independence.

regions.name: Nippes
regions.title: Nippes
text: Nippes (French, pronounced [nip] ) or Nip (Haitian Creole) is one of the ten departments (the highest-level political subdivisions) of Haiti located in southern Haiti. It is the most recently created department, having been split from Grand'Anse in 2003. The capital of the department is Miragoâne, and it is the least populous department in Haiti.
